   257	## Read-Only Reviewer Mode (`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1`)
   258	
   259	The command classes above describe ownership coordination between *owner sessions*. A separate
   260	concern is **advisory external reviewers**: external Claude/Codex/Gemini processes delegated
   261	to inspect artifacts and return structured findings as text — they are not Proofbound gate
   262	reviewers and must not write lifecycle evidence directly.
   263	
   264	`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` is an opt-in guard for these advisory reviewer processes. It
   265	layers on top of the `CommandPolicy` / owner-lease architecture:
   266	
   267	- The guard runs **before** `enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate` and before preCommand hooks, so a
   268	  readonly reviewer cannot acquire an owner lease, use `--takeover`, or trigger any hook
   269	  side-effect that requires mutating access.
   270	- Only `ownershipClass === 'readOnly'` commands (e.g. `session_brief`, `story_get`,
   271	  `checklist_get`, `finding_list`) proceed. All other classes fail closed.
   272	- This mode does **not** change how normal Proofbound gate reviewers (`lattice-review-*`) work,
   273	  but their evidence authority depends on the invocation path. A registered host adapter can
   274	  issue a signed, exact native-review invocation attestation; that broker-attested native
   275	  reviewer may call `review_pass_set`, `finding_add`, or `delivery_check_set` directly. A

   277	  current HEAD/material/story-files binding; `delivery_check_set` consumes a one-shot
   278	  descriptor capability for that exact dispatch immediately before persistence. Merely

A malformed array or duplicate executable+argv identity fails closed to that default. The command-specific ceiling never bypasses the outer CLI deadline or its TERM→KILL→reap cleanup. Within one `verification_evidence_batch_add`, exact cwd+command duplicates share one execution, while every intent still evaluates its own immutable selector and receives its own receipt; any failed selector preserves the all-or-nothing checklist write.
+
 `doctor` also outputs `Runtime scan:`, which is not process gate evidence but a runtime-environment drift check. Runtime facts are defined in `packages/main/src/core/runtime-fact-registry.ts` and protected by `scripts/verify-runtime-fact-contract.mjs`, covering worktree entrypoint authority, the CLI entrypoint, the global `@lattice/core` realpath, the project-local `node_modules/.bin/lattice`, the Node/package version, the validate source, and `external-reference-policy`. External projects receive only warn/advisory and are never hard-failed because of the Orchestrate repo's own symlink expectations. `external-reference-policy` scans only `lattice.config.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, and `docs/requirements/**/*.md`, excluding story/fixture/build/source-comment noise; it reports only a policy warning and does not assert a connectivity pass.
 
 Proofbound runtime artifacts are a separate table: `packages/main/src/core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts` defines the ignore, materialHash, and repair semantics for runtime files such as `.lattice/activity.jsonl`, legacy `docs/story/activity.jsonl`, `.lattice/runtime/`, `.lattice/traces/`, `.lattice-serve.json`, and debug/browser logs. `lattice init` merges missing runtime ignore rules into the existing `.gitignore`; `lattice doctor` reports runtime artifacts already tracked by git, and on `--repair` runs `git rm --cached` only for paths the registry marks as repairable. These files do not make materialHash-backed verification evidence stale; `.lattice/story/` is process evidence and is not treated as a runtime artifact.
 
 DONE merges also maintain a separate non-runtime artifact release provenance ledger at `.lattice/artifact-releases.jsonl`. It records releasable `docs/**` and `experiments/**` contents by normalized path and deterministic `sha256:` artifact-set digest, excluding `.lattice/story/**` lifecycle metadata and watched CLI/runtime build inputs. This ledger is provenance only: it does not activate a package release and does not broaden CLI patch semver bump rules.

1-# Review-Run Binding Race — relax id-recency, keep material/scope/empty-hash guards
2-
3-## Problem
4:When reviewer lanes run in parallel, or a reviewer retries review_run_start, a second run_start on the same (storyId, lane) in the same reviewRound mints a newer reviewRunId. currentRunForLane (review-run.ts) returns the newest-by-recency run, and any review_pass_set / finding_add bound to the ORIGINAL run is hard-rejected — at write time by assertCurrentReviewRunForEvidence (review-run.ts:669-672, "is not the current latest reviewer run") and at validate time by validateEvidenceRunBinding (review-run.ts:794-804, issue 'stale_run') — purely because a newer run exists, even though the bound run is still in the current round and still material- and scope-fresh. This empties the lane's valid-pass set and stalls quorum_submit (handlers/quorum-submit.ts), which forced a whole fresh REVIEW round during B-70e4. reviewerWrite is lease-exempt (command-policy.ts) and review_run_start vs review_pass_set/finding_add hold DISTINCT mkdir locks, so the owner lease never serialized these writers; B-77ed only raised the lock budget to 30s, which does not address the false-reject.
5-
6-## Decision
7-Remove the id-recency rejection: a non-latest run is ACCEPTED when it is still material-fresh and scope-fresh, and rejected only by the existing freshness and scope checks (stale-by-material/scope, never stale-merely-by-id). The validate-side relax is KIND-AWARE: the 'stale_run' issue is dropped only for evidence.kind === 'pass' (so a material-fresh non-latest PASS becomes valid), but KEPT for findings so an older OPEN finding is still surfaced and not hidden by a newer pass on the same lane (collectReviewerEvidenceState supersedes it only once the finding is resolved/dismissed). This is conditioned on a mandatory soundness guard added to checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit: the storyFilesHash drift-advisory downgrade must treat EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH (sha256 of an empty story-owned diff) as no-signal on BOTH the stored and the live side and fall through to strict materialHash, exactly as delivery-check-hash.ts:184-188 already does. The lease-contract doc (session-ownership-and-write-leases.md) is reconciled doc-only.

     4	Source story: B-503b
     5	Source proposal: DDP-001
     6	Created: 2026-06-19
     7	
     8	## Decision
     9	
    10	Proofbound should add a mandatory review assurance floor for code-changing stories: ordinary code diffs require at least one review round before DONE, failure or bug signals escalate to three local single-host rounds, and high-risk lifecycle/gate/Authority/process-fact work keeps the stronger three-round two-host or explicit degraded-single-host path.
    11	
    12	## Context
    13	
    14	A small development task can look low risk during PLAN but still ship a bug when it reaches DONE with no review floor. Existing review escalation is threshold-triggered by first REVIEW round countable findings, which is useful but does not prevent zero-review code closure. This plan documents the missing floor and the escalation rule without implementing runtime code in this story.
    15	
    16	## Scope
    17	
    18	Applies to future Proofbound CLI lifecycle policy and DONE closure design for code-changing stories. This document is a planning and policy artifact only; runtime DONE oracle implementation, storage fields, and exact row ids are future work.
    19	
    20	## Non-Goals
    21	
    22	- Do not force every code-changing story into three rounds by default.
    23	- Do not weaken existing review_escalation_status, decision_doc_quorum_check, or DONE gates.
    24	- Do not claim local 3x1 review is two-host independent review.
    25	- Do not claim Authority completion without verified Authority Server gate_decision receipts.
    26	- Do not implement runtime gate code in this story.
    27	
    28	## Options Considered
    29	
    30	### Force every code change through three local single-host rounds
    31	
    32	Pros:
    33	- Simple to explain
    34	- Stronger than one-round review for every code diff
    35	
    36	Cons:
    37	- Over-applies heavy review to clean small changes
    38	- Raises token and time cost without requiring a real failure signal
    39	
    40	### Keep current threshold-triggered review escalation only
    41	
    42	Pros:
    43	- No new policy or implementation work
    44	- Preserves current lifecycle behavior
    45	
    46	Cons:
    47	- Does not solve zero-review code DONE
    48	- Misses low-risk-looking tasks that only reveal bugs after implementation
    49	
    50	### Require full 3x2 for every code change
    51	
    52	Pros:
    53	- Maximal independent review assurance
    54	- Reduces reliance on single-host judgment
    55	
    56	Cons:
    57	- Too expensive for ordinary small code changes
    58	- Can block local development when a second host is unavailable
    59	
    60	## Chosen Approach
    61	
    62	Introduce a review assurance floor: zero-review code DONE is invalid; clean ordinary code requires at least one review round; real failure signals such as validation fail, bug, verified reviewer finding, post-DONE regression, or repeated rework make 3x1 local single-host audit sticky for closure; high-risk gate/Authority/lifecycle/process-fact work still requires 3x2 unless explicit degraded-single-host evidence is recorded.
    63	
    64	## Operational Rules
    65	
    66	- If a story has no material code diff, it may use the existing docs/typo/annotation policy for one-round low-risk review.
    67	- If a story has a material code diff, DONE must require at least one review round over the current material hash.
    68	- If a story records a validation fail, bug, verified reviewer finding, post-DONE regression, or repeated rework signal, DONE must require three rounds x one local host unless stronger policy requires 3x2.
    69	- Failure-triggered 3x1 escalation must be sticky for the story material until DONE or an explicit approved fallback supersedes it.
    70	- Lifecycle, gate, Authority, review, and process-fact work remains high-risk and should use three rounds x two hosts, or an explicit degraded-single-host fallback when policy allows.
    71	- Local host verdicts and degraded fallback evidence are Non-authority evidence and must not set authorityDone, fullAuthorityDone, or productionDone.
    72	- Future implementation must fail closed on stale material hash, missing host identity, missing prompt or validation binding, and duplicate/self-claimed assurance.
    73	
    74	## Local Diagnostic UX
    75	
    76	The local diagnostic surfaces are operator guidance only. They explain why a
    77	local DONE pre-check is blocked and which local commands refresh the evidence;
    78	they do not create remote proof, Authority receipt evidence, or a new completion
    79	capability.
    80	
    81	- `autopilot_review_status --storyId=<storyId>` may show all local run ids and
    82	  latest local run summaries, including counted and ignored host verdicts.
    83	- `review_escalation_status --storyId=<storyId>` may show
    84	  `voluntaryLocalRounds` even when escalation is not required. That visibility
    85	  must not change `required`, `ok`, or `assuranceLevel`.
    86	- A review-assurance DONE block should render `Stale material recovery` with:
    87	  `lattice validate --story=<storyId> --json`,
    88	  `lattice verification_evidence_refresh_stale --storyId=<storyId> --dryRun`
    89	  followed by the same command without `--dryRun` after rerunning listed
    90	  evidence commands, and `node bin/lattice.js autopilot_review_submit ... --materialDigest=<current-materialHash>`
    91	  for fresh local host verdicts.
    92	- The degraded-single-host writer guidance emits one executable worktree-local
    93	  `node bin/lattice.js autopilot_review_submit` command per required round; it
    94	  does not rely on a global `lattice` runtime that may resolve an older main
    95	  build. Each command uses explicit `--deriveBindings`, a real local
    96	  hostname/session identity, and the current material/story-files hashes. The
    97	  handler holds the story validation-execution lock keyed by the same canonical
    98	  metadata/runtime root used by validation writers (including wrapper-root
    99	  layouts) while applying the same
   100	  canonical PASS-admissibility predicate as the TEST gate: canonical command,
   101	  parseable `allPass`, current complete verification-coverage snapshot, no
   102	  blocking dirty paths, exact material/story-files identity, and exact-head or
   103	  trusted story-metadata-descendant lineage. It then derives the complete
   104	  canonical `keyId`/`validationDigest`/`promptDigest` envelope and persists the
   105	  single verdict plus process event before releasing the lock.
   106	  Any supplied binding mismatch fails before persistence. Omitting
   107	  `--deriveBindings` retains the legacy warning/non-counting behavior and does
   108	  not silently synthesize bindings.
   109	- Stale verification evidence and stale or ignored host verdicts remain
   110	  non-counting until refreshed or resubmitted over the current material hash.
   111	  The runbook must not suggest bypassing stale-material checks.
   112	
   113	## Verification Requirements
   114	
   115	- A future smoke test proves an ordinary code-diff story cannot reach DONE with zero review rounds.
   116	- A future smoke test proves a clean ordinary code-diff story can close after one valid review round.
   117	- A future smoke test proves validation failure or bug evidence makes 3x1 required and sticky before DONE.
   118	- A future smoke test proves high-risk lifecycle/gate/Authority/process-fact stories still require 3x2 or explicit degraded-single-host evidence.
   119	- A future smoke test proves 3x1 evidence reports assuranceLevel=degraded-single-host and never claims Authority Server receipt-backed completion.
   120	- A smoke test proves stale-material recovery text names stale local host
   121	  verdicts, truncates long ignored-verdict details, shows the validation,
   122	  stale-evidence refresh, and local verdict resubmission commands, and preserves
   123	  the local/non-authority boundary.
   124	- A smoke test proves the executable degraded guidance covers three distinct
   125	  one-host rounds, rejects stale/tampered bindings before write, and never
   126	  fabricates a second host or upgrades degraded assurance to 3x2.
   127	
   128	### Atomic local quorum persistence
   129	
   130	`quorum_submit` closes its bounded host-verdict batch as one immutable metadata
   131	transaction. It requires a clean entry HEAD/index/worktree, verifies that the
   132	`process-events.jsonl` delta contains exactly the invocation's `rounds × 2`
   133	`host_verdict` rows, runs normal commit hooks, and installs the exact metadata
   134	tree through a HEAD compare-and-swap. Pre-existing dirt is refused before any
   135	verdict write. Hook, content, or HEAD failures remove every generated verdict
   136	row and ignored local verdict file together; concurrent foreign bytes are
   137	preserved and reported rather than staged or overwritten. The assurance
   138	evaluator therefore consumes a durable complete quorum, never a partial dirty
   139	batch left by a failed closeout. `quorum_submit` owns this terminal completely:
   140	the CLI does not append a generic post-handler `codex_cli` row that would dirty
   141	the just-committed file. Same-material duplicate refusal reads committed
   142	`process-events.jsonl`, not the gitignored local verdict cache. Rollback removes
   143	only frozen event/JSON byte spans, preserving altered files and arbitrary
   144	foreign binary suffix bytes exactly.
   145	
   146	## Risks
   147	
   148	- Over-escalation could waste tokens if every source diff is treated as failure-triggered.
   149	- Under-escalation could persist if failure signals are not captured in a gate-consumed artifact.
   150	- Confusing 3x1 with two-host independence would overclaim review assurance.
   151	- Confusing local host verdicts with Authority receipts would violate the Authority boundary.
   152	
   153	## Supersession
   154	
   155	If this decision changes, update this file through a Proofbound story. Because
   156	this file is under `docs/requirements/decisions/*.md`, future edits should use
   157	the current story-lifecycle review escalation policy: direct decision-doc edits
   158	are diagnostic/classification inputs, and DONE requires 3x2 only when the
   159	review escalation trigger or an explicit high-risk policy requires it.

     5	## Purpose
     6	
     7	This document defines the execution plan for keeping Proofbound workflow commands
     8	host-neutral while limiting the Codex command surface to Codex adapter
     9	diagnostics and verification.
    10	
    11	The goal is not to add compatibility aliases for mistaken workflow commands.
    12	The goal is to stop generated prompts, generated assets, docs, and CLI
    13	suggestions from teaching agents that ordinary Proofbound lifecycle commands belong
    14	to a Codex-specific namespace.
    15	
    16	This plan follows four constraints:
    17	
    18	1. Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
    19	2. Do not optimize arbitrarily.
    20	3. Only fix real correctness issues.
    21	4. Preserve consistency of logic.
    22	
    23	## Problem Statement
    24	
    25	Proofbound is the workflow layer. It coordinates story state, checklist state,
    26	review artifacts, validation evidence, delivery checks, and convergence checks
    27	across hosts. Those commands must remain host-neutral.
    28	
    29	Codex is one possible host/adapter. Codex-specific commands may diagnose or
    30	verify Codex adapter assets, but they must not become a second namespace for
    31	ordinary Proofbound workflow operations.
    32	
    33	The operator-facing defect has two closely related forms:
    34	
    35	- A rejected namespace form can produce unclear suggestions if the executable
    36	  CLI is stale.
    37	- Generated Codex wrapper guidance can still encourage agents to run ordinary
    38	  workflow recovery commands through a Codex wrapper, which weakens the
    39	  host-neutral mental model even when the command technically works.
    40	
    41	The fix must clean guidance and preserve fail-closed command behavior.
    42	
    43	## Command Boundary Rule
    44	
    45	### Host-Neutral Workflow Commands
    46	
    47	The following command families belong to the Proofbound workflow layer and must be
    48	generated or recommended without a host or agent namespace:
    49	
    50	| Command family | Correct guidance |
    51	| --- | --- |
    52	| session recovery | `lattice session_brief` |
    53	| document discovery | `lattice aux_doc_list` |
    54	| story lifecycle | `lattice story_*` |
    55	| checklist updates | `lattice checklist_*` |
    56	| validation | `lattice validate` |
    57	| findings | `lattice finding_*` |
    58	| review artifacts | `lattice review_*` |
    59	| summary artifact | `lattice summary_set` |
    60	| delivery artifact | `lattice delivery_check_set` |
    61	| convergence | `lattice convergence_check` |
    62	
    63	Generated prompts may use the project-local wrapper form
    64	`node bin/lattice.js <command>` when local bootstrap is required. They must not
    65	route these commands through a Codex adapter wrapper.
    66	
    67	### Codex Adapter Commands
    68	
    69	The Codex command surface is limited to Codex adapter capabilities:
    70	
    71	| Purpose | Accepted guidance |
    72	| --- | --- |
    73	| Codex adapter diagnostics | `lattice codex doctor` or `lattice codex_doctor` |
    74	| Codex adapter verification evidence | `lattice codex verify` or `lattice verify_codex` |
    75	
    76	These commands are adapter-specific because they inspect or write evidence for
    77	Codex adapter assets, hooks, wrappers, manifests, and heartbeats.
    78	
    79	### Forbidden Generation Pattern
    80	
    81	Generators, docs, and prompt templates must not combine the Codex namespace
    82	prefix with ordinary workflow command families. In validation scripts, refer to
    83	this as the pattern:
    84	
    85	```text
    86	lattice\s+codex\s+(session_brief|aux_doc_list|story_|checklist_|validate|review_|finding_|summary_set|delivery_check_set|convergence_check)
    87	```
    88	
    89	Do not add aliases that make these forms succeed. Rejection is the correct
    90	behavior because the command boundary is part of the product model.
    91	
    92	## Current Fact Pattern
    93	
    94	The current source behavior already contains the correct narrow CLI fallback:
    95	
    96	- Codex adapter aliases for `verify` and `doctor` remain supported.
    97	- Codex-prefixed session recovery and document discovery are rejected.
    98	- The error message tells users to run the ordinary Proofbound command instead.

     1	# Proofbound LLM Usage Ledger Execution Plan
     2	
     3	> Story: B-1477
     4	> Scope: future execution plan only. This document does not implement source
     5	> code, provider logic, runtime registries, Authority Server behavior, or gate
     6	> behavior.
     7	
     8	## Problem Statement
     9	
    10	Proofbound can launch or coordinate work through multiple LLM-capable hosts, but it
    11	does not yet have one consistent place to record what each model call consumed,
    12	what budget decision was made before the call, and whether final usage came from
    13	the provider, from a local prompt-size estimate, or from no reliable source at
    14	all.
    15	
    16	Without a usage ledger, future budget decisions risk mixing three different
    17	facts:
    18	
    19	- true provider-reported usage returned by the model provider;
    20	- approximate prompt-size estimates made before or around a request;
    21	- unavailable usage when neither the provider nor a trusted adapter reports
    22	  counts.
    23	
    24	The ledger must keep these categories mechanically distinct. A local estimate is
    25	useful for preflight safety, but it is not billing truth, receipt truth, or
    26	Authority evidence.
    27	
    28	## Principles
    29	
    30	1. Do not optimize for optimization.
    31	2. Do not optimize arbitrarily.
    32	3. Only fix real correctness issues.
    33	4. Follow consistency of logic across providers, hosts, and Authority modes.
    34	5. Preserve the existing Proofbound boundary: local workflow evidence is local
    35	   unless a future receipt-backed Authority path explicitly promotes it.
    36	
    37	## Goals
    38	
    39	- Add a future JSONL ledger for LLM usage events that can be appended by local
    40	  Proofbound surfaces and, later, by receipt-backed Authority execution.
    41	- Represent true provider-reported usage, approximate prompt-size estimates, and
    42	  unavailable usage as separate states.
    43	- Support preflight and postflight budget decisions without treating estimates
    44	  as final usage.
    45	- Keep local Non-authority mode usable for ordinary Proofbound workflow while still
    46	  recording budget refusals and available usage facts.
    47	- Define the Authority Server receipt-backed path for future production
    48	  accounting without overclaiming local authority.
    49	- Prevent raw prompt, raw transcript, provider secret, customer API key, actor
    50	  key, and authorization header material from entering ledger records.
    51	
    52	## Non-Goals
    53	
    54	- No source code change in this story.
    55	- No provider adapter rewrite.
    56	- No pricing optimizer, model router, or arbitrary cost-saving feature.
    57	- No token-perfect estimator. Estimates are bounded diagnostics and preflight
    58	  guards only.
    59	- No new authority claim for ordinary Proofbound CLI, Codex, Claude, Gemini, local
    60	  runners, or host transcripts.
    61	- No replacement for signed `AuthorityReceipt` gate evidence.
    62	- No change to Authority Server receipt contracts in this story.
    63	
    64	## Usage Source Semantics
    65	
    66	The ledger record must carry a `usage.source` discriminator:
    67	
    68	| Source | Meaning | May count as final usage? | May satisfy Authority? |
    69	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    70	| `provider-reported` | The provider response included usage counters or billing-relevant units returned by the provider adapter. | Yes, for local budget accounting and display. | Only when embedded in a future signed evidence envelope and covered by a verified Authority receipt. |
    71	| `prompt-size-estimate` | Proofbound estimated prompt size before or around the request, using a local counter, tokenizer, bytes, or characters. | No. It may justify preflight refusal or warnings, but not final usage. | No. |
    72	| `unavailable` | No trusted provider usage and no accepted estimate are available. | No. It records absence explicitly. | No. |
    73	
    74	Rules:
    75	
    76	- Provider-reported usage wins over estimates for the same completed call.
    77	- Estimates must name the estimator and unit. They must not masquerade as
    78	  provider token counts.
    79	- Unavailable usage must be explicit, not represented as zero.
    80	- A failed request may still write a ledger entry if it consumed budget,
    81	  returned usage, or triggered a budget refusal.
    82	- Ledger readers must never infer that missing counts are zero-cost.
    83	
    84	### Estimate accuracy and fallback order
    85	
    86	`prompt-size-estimate` records must use the most accurate available estimator,
    87	in a strict, explicitly ordered fallback chain:
    88	
    89	1. **Provider `count_tokens` endpoint (preferred).** When the provider exposes a
    90	   token-counting endpoint, the estimate must prefer it. These counts are
    91	   model-version-specific: the same text tokenizes differently across model
    92	   versions, so the count must be requested for the exact target model.
    93	2. **Local tokenizer (fallback).** When the provider endpoint is unavailable,
    94	   fall back to a local tokenizer bound to the same provider/model family.
    95	3. **Bytes/characters heuristic (offline fallback only).** A bytes- or
    96	   character-based heuristic is the lowest-confidence fallback and is used only
    97	   when offline, i.e. when neither the provider endpoint nor a local tokenizer is
    98	   available. It must never be promoted to the preferred estimator.
    99	
   100	Every estimate record must:
   101	
   102	- record `usage.estimator.confidence` as `high | medium | low`, reflecting which
   103	  method was used (`high` for provider `count_tokens`, `medium` for a local
   104	  tokenizer, `low` for the bytes/chars heuristic);
   105	- bind the estimate to the exact `provider.model` it was computed for, because
   106	  token counts are model-version-specific and an estimate for one model version
   107	  must not be reused for another;
   108	- still record `usage.estimator.name`, `usage.estimator.version`, and
   109	  `usage.estimator.unit` alongside the new `confidence` field.
   110	
   111	### Streaming and failure usage capture
   112	
   113	Streaming responses report final usage differently from non-streaming responses,
   114	and a naive reader can lose the counts entirely:
   115	
   116	- For streaming responses, final usage must be read from the terminal stream
   117	  event (the final `message_delta` / final message that carries the completed
   118	  `usage` object), not assumed from a non-streaming response shape. The usage on
   119	  the terminal event is the authoritative provider-reported count for the call,
   120	  and it still qualifies as `usage.source=provider-reported`.
   540

   542

    31	## `host_run`
    32

    42	`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with

    44	run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:

    93	### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)
    94	
    95	| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
    96	|---|---|---|---|
    97	| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |

   100	In `--json` mode the bounded host transcript (at most 8 MiB per managed run) is
   101	delivered live on **stderr** so that **stdout stays clean** for the one JSON
   102	result. If the transcript exceeds that ceiling, the projection is explicitly
   103	truncated; the JSON `stdout` field carries only the bounded usage-parse tail,
   104	not an unbounded or complete transcript.
   105	
   106	If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
   107	but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
   108	`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
   109	`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
   110	downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
   111	delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
   112	event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async

   115	contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;

   259	## Binding conventions
   260	
   261	Every usage row carries the attribution passed to `host_run`:
   262	
   263	| Argument | Ledger field | Notes |
   264	|---|---|---|
   265	| `--storyId` | `storyId` | Canonical Story id. Omit for an adhoc run. |
   266	| `--agentType` | `agentType` | e.g. `reviewer`, `autopilot-repair`, `host-readiness-probe`. Required. |
   267	| `--phase` | `phase` | When omitted and `--storyId` is set, the phase resolves from the **configured story store** at call time (honoring a project's `storyDir`); an explicit `--phase` is used as-is and the store is never read. |
   268	| `--reviewRunId` | `threadId` | e.g. `B-xxxx:RR-001`. Joins rows against `review-runs.json`. |
   269	| `--lane` | `subagentId` | e.g. `lattice-review-quality`. |
   270	
   271	`--reviewRunId` must start with `<storyId>:` when `--storyId` is given, so a
   272	ledger row can never silently mis-join across stories — a mismatch is refused
   273	before any host is spawned. Omitting `--reviewRunId` / `--lane` leaves
   274	`threadId` / `subagentId` null (no empty-string pollution).

   276	When `--storyId` is given **without** `--phase`, the phase is resolved through the
   277	configured story store; a story unknown to that store is refused pre-spawn. When
   278	`--phase` is supplied the store is never consulted, so `--phase` works with or
   279	without `--storyId` even in a project whose story metadata lives under a
   280	custom `storyDir`.
   281	
   282	## Per-host usage semantics
   283	
   284	Provider truth is preferred over estimates; an absence is recorded as an explicit
   285	`source=unavailable`, never a fabricated zero.
   286	
   287	- **codex** — parses the terminal `turn.completed` usage event from
   288	  `codex exec --json` and maps it to `{ input: input_tokens - cached_input_tokens,
   289	  cacheRead: cached_input_tokens, cacheCreation: null, output: output_tokens }`.
   290	  The `input` field is the **uncached remainder** (codex `input_tokens` includes
   291	  cached input); the original payload (including `reasoning_output_tokens`) is
   292	  digested raw.
   293	- **claude** — parses the stream-json `result` envelope usage via
   294	  `parseClaudeCliOutput` (the four-field Anthropic usage plus the served model).
   295	
   296	A parse miss (no `turn.completed` event, no `result` usage) records an
   297	`unavailable` final with a reason rather than inventing counts.
   298	
   299	同样的诚实口径适用于 reviewer A/B：缺少 exact per-role historical envelope、
   300	reviewer output、adjudication bytes 或 provider receipt 时结果是
   301	`INCONCLUSIVE`，不是“0 token”或已证明的节省。B-235e 的独立 replay campaign
   302	因此不声称达到计划中的 50% incremental / 40% assembled 降幅。
   303	
   304	The one-line usage summary reflects the **actual append outcome**, not merely
   305	that the provider envelope parsed. When the ledger append itself fails (a corrupt
   306	ledger, or a lock-wait timeout that skips the write), the summary reports a
   307	skipped state (`recorded: none`, reason `ledger_append_failed(...)`) and the
   308	stderr line reads `usage: ledger_append_failed(...)` — it never claims
   309	`usage recorded` for a row that never landed. This applies to both managed hosts;
   310	the provider is still surfaced for attribution, but token counts stay null. A
   311	provider record that BUILT fine but whose append failed is reported as an
   312	append failure keyed on the parsed usage — it is **never degraded to
   313	`source=unavailable`** (which would falsely read as "the provider reported
   314	nothing"), and no second `unavailable` final is attempted for it.
   315	
   316	The same honesty gate covers the **blocked rows**: a cap refusal claims
   317	`recorded: blocked` (and, for a concurrency refusal, surfaces the blocked row's
   318	`recordId`) only when the blocked row **actually appended**. When that append is
   319	swallowed too, the refusal itself is unchanged — still fail-closed, no spawn,
   320	non-zero exit — but the summary reports `recorded: none` with `recordId: null`
   321	and a composed reason that keeps the refusal visible, e.g.
   322	`hard_budget_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)` or
   323	`concurrency_cap_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)`. A recordId is never
   324	minted for a blocked row that never persisted.
   325	
   326	## Provider execution surfaces
   327	
   328	Every production provider spawn site carries a `ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus`
   329	and is enumerated by `provider-execution-inventory-contract`, which fails if a
   330	new spawn path appears unclassified:
   331	
   332	- `managed` — runs through ManagedHostRun (durable run identity, supervised
   333	  process group, absolute deadline, one terminal receipt).
   334	- `admission_only` — not managed-executed, but still routed through the shared
   335	  admission boundary, so the concurrency cap below applies.
   336	- `adapter_only` — a low-level adapter whose caller owns admission.
   337	- `readiness_probe` — version/readiness checks only; never review evidence.
   338	- `legacy_unmanaged` — neither managed nor admission-routed. Reserved and
   339	  **currently empty by contract**: the inventory test asserts no surface uses
   340	  it, so introducing one is a deliberate, reviewable act.
   341	
   342	There is no `admission_managed` status — admission and managed execution are
   343	independent properties, spelled `admission_only` and `managed`.
   344	
   345	See `docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md` for
   346	the decision record.
   347	
   348	## Caps (fail-closed, before spawn)
   349	
   350	With the usage ledger enabled, both caps run at the choke point BEFORE a host
   351	is spawned, and each refusal attempts to record a
   352	`decision.kind=blocked` ledger row (diagnostics-honest; an append failure is
   353	reported as `recorded: none`). With `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0`, budget enforcement
   354	and every ledger row are disabled; the provider-process capacity admission
   355	still runs before every spawn and refuses fail-closed without claiming a
   356	blocked row was persisted.
   357	
   358	- **Per-dispatch hard budget** — reuses the existing `LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS`
   359	  preflight guard per call. An over-budget preflight estimate refuses with
   360	  `reasonCode hard_budget_exceeded` before spawning.
   361	- **Provider-process concurrency** — a shared slot registry under
   362	  `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/`
   363	  holds **fixed numbered slots** `slot-0.json` .. `slot-(cap-1).json`, one per
   364	  live run (pid + `startedAt` + an acquire-minted **ownership token**).
   365	  Admission and reclaim are serialized by the ownership-checked provider
   366	  registry lock, then the selected fixed slot is created with exclusive `wx`.
   367	  The lock makes the live-count check, stale reclaim, cap-lowering check and
   368	  create one cross-process transaction, so simultaneous starts and corrupt-slot
   369	  replacement cannot slip past the cap. When every index
   370	  under `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default **4**; unset / invalid /
   371	  `<=0` falls back to the default; an explicit larger value is honored) is
   372	  held, the run refuses fail-closed with a non-zero exit, prints the live-run
   373	  list, and, when the ledger is enabled, writes a blocked row with `reasonCode
   374	  concurrency_cap_exceeded`.
   375	  Slot reclaim is **ownership-aware** (mirroring the ledger-lock doctrine
   376	  below): a slot with a recorded **dead pid** is reclaimed at any age; a slot
   377	  whose metadata is **missing/corrupt** (the holder crashed between creating
   378	  the file and its metadata landing) is reclaimed once its mtime exceeds the
   379	  `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_SLOT_STALE_MS` orphan backstop (default **6h**); a slot
   380	  with a **live** recorded pid is **never reclaimed by age** — a long host run
   381	  keeps its admission and waiters refuse at cap. Reclaim re-verifies the
   382	  occupant immediately before the unlink under the same registry lock and then
   383	  re-creates exclusively, so a crashed run never wedges the cap and a racing
   384	  reclaimer cannot delete a slot a new holder just re-acquired. Slot release on
   385	  exit is best-effort, registry-serialized and **token-guarded**:
   386	  the file is unlinked only while it still carries the releasing run's own
   387	  token, so a reclaimed-and-re-acquired slot survives the original holder's
   388	  late release. Raising the cap mid-flight exposes more indexes; lowering it
   389	  counts every live high-index slot and refuses new starts until the total live
   390	  count drops below the new cap.
   391	
   392	Blocked rows are provider-honest: a refusal records the provider of the managed
   393	host that was asked to run (`openai` for codex or `anthropic` for claude), never
   394	a hard-coded default.
   395	
   396	The autopilot Claude repair launch (`lattice autopilot execute
   397	--allowClaudeRepair`) passes the **same pre-spawn admission** in both ledger
   398	modes. With the ledger ON, budget and capacity refusals can also write the
   399	diagnostic blocked row. With the ledger OFF there are no usage rows or budget
   400	guard, but capacity admission remains mandatory and the slot is still released
   401	after the run.
   402	
   403	The `cross_host_review` Codex leaf runs through ManagedHostRun and the same
   404	provider admission (provider `openai`). It supports detach/resume by exact
   405	`managedRunId`, never spawns a replacement on resume, and binds the terminal
   406	`receiptId` into host-B verdict provenance. Budget/cap/provider failures still
   407	produce an honest blocked/error decision; raw stdout is never gate evidence.
   408	
   409	Concurrent runs' ledger appends are serialized by a cross-process lock at the
   410	writer choke point (an atomic `llm-usage.jsonl.lock/` directory with a bounded
   411	wait), so parallel host runs can never interleave appends and break the ledger
   412	hash chain — a writer that cannot acquire the lock in time skips its append
   413	(an honest under-count) rather than corrupting the chain. Lock reclaim is
   414	ownership-aware: the acquirer records `owner.json` (holder pid + a unique
   415	release token) inside the lock dir, and a held lock is reclaimed only when
   416	that pid is dead, or — for an ownerless/corrupt lock, i.e. the holder crashed
   417	between creating the dir and recording ownership — when the dir mtime exceeds
   418	the `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_MS` orphan backstop. A live holder is
   419	never reclaimed no matter how long it holds the lock (slow filesystem, GC
   420	pause, suspension); release removes the lock only while `owner.json` still
   421	carries the releaser's own token.
   422	
   423	There is **no queuing** in this story: over the cap means refuse, not wait.
   424	
   425	Set `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0` to disable usage preflight/budget/final rows. It
   426	does **not** disable ManagedHostRun ownership or provider-process admission.
   427	
   428	## Diagnostics, cleanup, and trust boundary
   429	
   430	`lattice doctor --full` lists every managed run with state, worker liveness,
   431	worker heartbeat, provider progress mode/time, deadline, cancellation,
   432	residual-process status, `replacementSafe`, and retention state. `lattice
   433	doctor --repair` removes heavy terminal run directories only after the 90-day
   434	retention window and first revalidates sealed spec, result, event-journal,
   435	proposal and evidence-binding digests, then archives the sealed receipt,
   436	evidence-binding digest, binding projection, provider-authored proposal body,
   437	and import-seal pair under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. On recover,
   438	the proposal body is re-digested against the sealed receipt's
   439	evidenceProposalDigest, the binding body is re-digested against the archive's
   440	evidenceBindingDigest, and the archived seal's schemaVersion, runId, and
   441	bindingDigest are checked the same way as the live path. A pre-existing
   442	receipt archive is kept only when that complete capture is valid. An
   443	incomplete crash leftover or pre-F-127 archive whose receiptId matches is
   444	atomically replaced from still-valid live artifacts; if neither side can
   445	form a complete archive, GC reports corrupt and retains the live runtime
   446	instead of deleting it. Heavy live-output
   447	and result provider text are not retained. Active or
   448	corrupt runs and any directory still carrying one-shot inputs are retained
   449	fail-closed for inspection; failed launch/claim paths erase prompt, capability,
   450	and one-shot environment immediately. The imported binding carries a separate
   451	immutable digest seal, so a shape-preserving binding rewrite is corrupt before
   452	doctor/GC can delete it. Expired cross-host runs also remove only their canonical
   453	`lattice-xhr-review-*/worktree` snapshot; paths outside that tmp boundary fail
   454	closed. Per-run live output is capped at 8 MiB;
   455	status readers page bounded frames and surface truncation rather than loading an
   456	unbounded transcript.
   457	
   458	The runtime directory is local and mode 0700; sensitive one-shot files are 0600.
   459	This protects against other users under ordinary filesystem permissions, not a
   460	same-UID/root attacker. Operators must treat retained live output as locally
   461	sensitive. Native Codex/Claude subagent APIs are deliberately out of scope:
   462	ManagedHostRun owns only cross-provider CLI processes launched by Proofbound.
   463	
   464	## `usage_sweep` (read-only retro-attribution)
   465	
   466	```
   467	lattice usage_sweep --since 2026-07-01 [--json]
   468	```
   469	
   470	`usage_sweep` stream-reads `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and
   471	`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` since a cutoff and reports per-session token
   472	totals, originator (desktop vs exec vs claude-code), cwd, first/last timestamps,
   473	and `B-xxxx` story mentions, plus a per-story rollup and grand totals. It exists
   474	to make runs that never went through `host_run` (interactive desktop sessions in
   475	particular) at least visible.
   476	
   477	- The report header states **NON-AUTHORITATIVE ESTIMATE** prominently in both
   478	  the human table and `--json`. The totals come from host transcript stores, not
   479	  billing truth.
   480	- It performs **no ledger backfill**: swept sessions are never written into the
   481	  usage ledger.
   482	- It is strictly **read-only**. The only write it can perform is an explicit
   483	  `--out <path>` JSON report, and that write is create-only and fenced:
   484	  - `--out` must be a **relative** path that resolves inside the project root;
   485	    absolute paths and any `..` traversal escaping the root are refused
   486	    outright.
   487	  - It only ever **creates a new report file** — the file is opened with the
   488	    exclusive-create `wx` flag, so an already-existing target is refused
   489	    atomically and `usage_sweep` can never overwrite or truncate anything
   490	    (not even via a symlink at the target path).
   491	  - It refuses to write through **symlinked ancestor directories**, and the
   492	    resolved real path must still fall inside the (realpath'd) project root,
   493	    so an inside-root symlink cannot redirect the report outside the project.
   494	  - Missing report directories are created only **after** all of those checks
   495	    pass.
   496	  - Because `--out` writes a file into the material tree, a **non-empty `--out`
   497	    is dynamically classified `storyScopedMutating`** by the ownership gate
   498	    (F-014), so it is refused in read-only reviewer mode
   499	    (`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1`) and on a retired root; without `--out`,
   500	    `usage_sweep` stays read-only and runnable by any session.
   501	  - The **same `--out` boundary governs the CLI activity / hook layer** (F-028):
   502	    a plain (no-`--out`) `usage_sweep` is read-only there too, so it runs **no
   503	    pre/post command hooks** and writes **no activity-log entry by default** (the
   504	    `LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY=1` read-only heartbeat override documented
   505	    in docs/CLI.md still applies); a non-empty `--out` is treated as a write and
   506	    runs the hooks + records activity like any other mutating command.
   507	  - The same boundary also governs the **codex process-event surface** (F-032):
   508	    under `LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex` cli-engine appends a `codex_cli` event
   509	    to the active story's `process-events.jsonl` after a command. That append is
   510	    STORY metadata, so it obeys the identical read-only contract — a plain
   511	    (no-`--out`) `usage_sweep` appends **no process event** (even with an
   512	    inferred active story), while a non-empty `--out` (a write) records the
   513	    process event like any other mutating command. The owner-lease heartbeat is
   514	    intentionally exempt: it is keyed on the ownership class (only a
   515	    `storyScopedMutating`/`dangerousMutating` write touches the lease), never on
   516	    this read-only classification, so read-only session upkeep is unaffected.
   517	
   518	## Non-goals
   519	
   520	- Usage rows **never gate the workflow** — they are `gateEvidence=false`
   521	  diagnostics and are not consumed by any REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority gate.
   522	- Interactive desktop host sessions are **out of reach** of the choke point;
   523	  they are report-only via `usage_sweep`, never through `host_run`.
   524	- `usage_sweep` never mutates story, ledger, or lifecycle state and never
   525	  backfills the ledger.
